ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory enhanced due diligence under Article 6 AMLA and FINMA Circular 2016/07. Screening must cover the United Nations consolidated sanctions list, Swiss SECO sanctions lists, United States OFAC SDN list, EU consolidated financial sanctions list, and UK sanctions list. Politically exposed persons (PEPs) — both domestic and foreign — require senior management approval and enhanced ongoing monitoring. Beneficial owners with direct or indirect ownership of 25% or more, or control via other means, must be positively identified and verified against continuously updated sanction and PEP databases before incorporation proceeds.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Zefix – Zentraler Firmenindex (central business names index of the Swiss Commercial Register Office, operated by the Federal Institute of Intellectual Property and cantonal commercial registries)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The corporate name must be in one of the official Swiss languages (German, French, Italian, or Romansh) and must be written in Latin characters. For names derived from non-Latin scripts, an official transliteration into Latin script is mandatory; the transliterated name becomes the registered name. The name must comply with Article 950 CO, be truthful, and not induce error. Non-Latin auxiliary names may be added only as a supplementary element and must be clearly distinguishable from the official registered name.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: The name reservation is issued by the cantonal commercial register authority after a preliminary examination. A rejected name may be refiled immediately with additional supporting evidence. An administrative appeal must be lodged with the competent cantonal administrative court within 30 days of receipt of the rejection decision. The appeal must detail the grounds why the proposed name complies with Article 950 CO and why it does not conflict with existing names or protected trademarks.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Lawful with restrictions. A Swiss AG must maintain a registered office in the canton of incorporation with a valid physical address for legal service and communication. A registered agent or professional domiciliation provider offering virtual-office services is permissible, provided it includes genuine physical premises, mail handling, and corporate records access. For a high-reputation real-time video-matching platform, reliance on a pure virtual address without operational substance may be scrutinized during tax and regulatory reviews.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Swiss Federal Act on the Amendment of the Swiss Civil Code (Code of Obligations, OR/CO), Part One: Book of Obligations, Articles 620–763 (Stock Company / Aktiengesellschaft), Articles 640 and 650 (Minimum Capital and Share Subscription), and Article 716b (Non-Transferable Duties of the Board). Also apply the Swiss Code of Civil Procedure (ZPO) for notarization protocols and the Swiss Ordinance on the Commercial Register (HRegV, SR 221.411).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Commercial Register Office of the Canton of Zug (Handelsregisteramt des Kantons Zug), operating under the Swiss Federal Commercial Register Office (Eidgenössisches Handelsregisteramt / Registre fédéral du commerce)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Public Deed of Incorporation (Statut / Gründungsurkunde) and the Articles of Association (Statuten / Statuts), submitted via the Swiss Commercial Register application portal
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum issued capital for an Aktiengesellschaft is CHF 100,000; paid-up capital must be at least 20% (CHF 20,000). In the case of contributions in kind, a sworn auditor's report (Sachgründungsbericht) is required. The capital must be deposited in a Swiss cantonal bank or licensed bank in the name of the company and confirmed via bank blocking confirmation (Blockierungsbestätigung / Sperrkonto) until registration in the Commercial Register.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the company confirms the subscription of share capital in the amount of CHF 100,000 issued as registered shares, with shares in the name of the subscribers and at least CHF 20,000 fully paid in prior to registration. RESOLVED, that the registered office is adopted as provided in Article 1 of the Articles of Association for the Canton of Zug, and that the company designates the authorized representatives required for Commercial Register filing. RESOLVED, that the persons named at this first board meeting are appointed as chairman and members of the Board of Directors, with signing authority of individual or joint signature per the official list. The Board is authorized to execute all filings, engage the external auditor, and carry out the formation formalities.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Swiss Commercial Register Office of the Canton of Zug (Handelsregisteramt des Kantons Zug)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the proposed company name plus 'AG' for a preliminary name search through the cantonal Commercial Register office or the Swiss Central Business Name Index. Verify that the name complies with Art. 950 OR, does not mislead (Täuschungsschutz), and is sufficiently distinct within the same register territory. Apply for non-binding name reservation where permissible to secure the name prior to deed drafting.
required_dossiers: Proposed company name (max three components)
Statement of business purpose (Zweck)
Canton of registered office
Confirmation of no existing identical or misleading names
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused, submit an amended name for reconsideration; if the new name is also refused, file an objection under Art. 956 OR within 30 days of the official registration refusal with the cantonal Commercial Register Appeals Commission and, ultimately, the Federal Commercial Register Office.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarial Public Deed of Incorporation and Adoption of Articles
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Swiss Notary Public (Notariat Zug) and the Commercial Register Office for registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the incorporators before a Swiss notary for the execution of the public deed. The deed must include the Articles of Association, name, business purpose, capital, registered office, appointment of the Board, and the types of shares. Notarize that contributions in kind or against a current account receivable (for ad-hoc video matching and social telephony digital assets) are fully described, and that the share capital is fully subscribed and paid in as required by law. The notary files the deed and supporting documents with the Cantonal Commercial Register.
required_dossiers: Public deed of incorporation dated and signed before the notary
Articles of Association (Statuten) signed by the incorporation party
Certified identification documents (passport or Swiss ID) of all incorporators
Bank blocking confirmation for minimum capital payment (Sperrkonto), or audit report for contributions in kind
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary identifies deficiencies, the incorporators can remedy them by signing an amending notarial deed or supplementary certificate. If the notary requires the mandatory Swiss auditor (statutory auditor) to validate the capital report, the applicant can cure the deficiency by engaging a licensed auditor and submitting the revised report before a second notarial execution.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Bank Blocking Confirmation or Payment In Kind Report
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cantonal Bank or licensed Swiss Bank; for in-kind contributions, a licensed Swiss statutory auditor
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a blocked capital account in the company's name with a Swiss bank. Deposit the minimum paid-up capital (CHF 100,000, of which at least CHF 20,000 is paid-in; or the entire capital if no further calls are made). Instruct the bank to issue a blocking confirmation addressed to the notary and the Commercial Register. For contributions in kind (e.g., video chat software system, patent, trademark), prepare a sworn report on the valuation of non-cash contributions.
required_dossiers: Bank blocking confirmation (Blockierungsbestätigung) stating the CHF 100,000 nominal capital is credited and blocked
Power of attorney for the bank account (if opened via agents)
For contributions in kind: valuation report, financial statements of the contributing company where necessary
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank refuses to release the blocking confirmation due to AML/KYC deficiencies, provide enhanced beneficial ownership information. If the Chapter of the Commercial Register questions the valuation of a non-cash contribution, remedy by obtaining a supplementary expert valuation report under Art. 635 OR and submit it in notarially certified form.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Appointment of Board of Directors, Corporate Purpose Compliance Review, and Authorization Statement
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors of the company and the Commercial Register Office of the Canton of Zug
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold the first board meeting and adopt the first board resolution resolving the subscription of shares, the adoption of the registered office, the appointment of the chairman and board members, and establishing authorized signatories. The board must verify that the statutory purpose includes 'online video match-making and content-based social networking platforms' and the operation of ancillary digital services, which falls under the ISIC 6311 Data Processing, Hosting and Related Activities umbrella, thereby requiring no industry-specific federal licensing. Make the declaration on voting rights and ensure accurate disclosure of the ultimate beneficial owner for anti-money laundering registry purposes.
required_dossiers: Minutes of the first board meeting
List of directors (Name, Address, Nationality, Date of Birth)
Declaration of acceptance of the office by each director
List of authorized representatives and signing authority
Statutory declaration of business purpose congruence with the commercial register entry
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Commercial Register questions the appointment formalities or the business purpose wording, cure the issue via a written board resolution clarifying the company's operations and file a compliant declaration. If a director lacks Swiss criminal record clearance or has been disqualified, the board substitutes the director and notarizes the revised list of directors.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Commercial Register Registration and Legal Entity Perfection
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial Register Office of the Canton of Zug acting under Federal Commercial Register provisions
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After notarization and the board resolutions, the notary or principal submits the complete registration dossier through the Swiss Commercial Register portal (Zefix / Handelsregister). Registration is perfected when the Commercial Register issues its order and publishes in the Swiss Official Gazette of Commerce (SHAB). The issuance is the legal constitutive act and forms the legal person. After registration, apply for the Swiss VAT number and obtain tax/company registration extracts for the purposes of corporate tax obligations.
required_dossiers: Notarized public deed of incorporation
Articles of Association
Declaration that paid-up capital is at the disposal of the company
Bank blocking confirmation or in-kind contribution report
Appointment documents of board and signatories
Registration application form HRegV
Consent of the external auditor if statutory audit waiver not sought
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Commercial Register requires additional evidence, supplementary declarations can be submitted through a notarially certified curative filing. If the registration order is refused or appealed, the applicant can file a complaint with the cantonal Commercial Register supervisory authority (Oberaufsicht) and subsequent appeal to the Swiss Federal Administrative Court under applicable procedures.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Video Telephony and Social Network Operational Terms Compliance Check
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Federal Office for Communications (OFCOM) and the Federal Data Protection and Information Commissioner (FDPIC)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Although the video chat social app does not require a broadcasting or telecommunications license, the company must verify that its services are classified as information society services under Swiss law. Review lawful interception obligations under the LeiSurveillance (BÜPF). Prepare technical compliance documentation for end-to-end encryption and age verification to prevent unlawful content. The company must implement cookie and user consent protocols reflecting GDPR-aligned Swiss FADP (DSG), which is particularly relevant for video data processing.
required_dossiers: Internal telecom and video service classification note
Data process inventory (Records of Processing Activities) under DSG
Age verification and moderation policy for live random video pairing
Terms of Service manual
Minimum technical security statement for cipher and transmission protocols
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If OFCOM initiates an inquiry into whether the service constitutes a telecommunication service requiring licensing, file a legal classification memorandum demonstrating the B2C software and pure transmission/protocol capabilities of the platform and the absence of dedicated infrastructure. If user complaints arise before the FDPIC, rectify by implementing new data minimization settings and appointing a Swiss representative for data subjects.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Federal Office for the Environment (FOEN / Bundesamt für Umwelt, BAFU) — Environmental Affairs Section of the Canton of Zug (Amt für Umwelt)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: not_applicable — virtual video communication service with no physical industrial premises. Mandatory DEES requirements: WBG, legal obligations under the Act on Environmental Protection (Umweltschutzgesetz, USG) do not apply; no vessel wastewater, no regulated TPU emission sources; internal measure on the use of green data centers and energy consumption should be voluntary or be aligned with the Federal requirements if servers are co-located.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: A computerized service operator has no physical manufacturing plant. Business and office premises in Zug must comply with cantonal fire safety assurance (Feuerpolizei, feu control certificates), structural load safety, and occupational health inspection for continuous work at workstations. If the company sets up a physical office in the Canton of Zug, it must obtain a General Compliance of Works procedures and LIFE Safety Evacuation certificate from the municipal authorities, complete Workplace Lighting/Noise/LCD Screen Compliance, and ensure first-aid procedures per Swiss workplace security ordinances. The building owner must submit a fire safety concept and, where VDP-NL (video data processing and non-licensed office), the workspace contractor must provide a workstation risk assessment before hiring employees.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Swiss National Bank (SNB) / Schweizerische Nationalbank, acting together with the Federal Department of Finance (FDF) and the Swiss Financial Market Supervisory Authority (FINMA) in the areas of monetary policy, payment-system oversight, and banking supervision.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Swiss franc is fully convertible under Article VIII of the IMF Articles of Agreement. Switzerland maintains no exchange-control legislation and draws no legal distinction between current-account and capital-account convertibility. Dividends, profit repatriation, repayment of shareholder loans, royalties, interest and liquidation proceeds may be transferred abroad freely and without prior approval. However, sanctions and embargoes administered by SECO (State Secretariat for Economic Affairs), OFAC extraterritorial enforcement, and FINMA AML obligations can materially delay or block payments where a sanctioned person, entity, or jurisdiction is involved or where the underlying funds are suspected to be illicit. For a cross-border video-match social app, treasury planning must therefore centre on sanctions screening, revenue-source traceability, and robust documentation rather than exchange-control pleading.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Switzerland does not impose any statutory timeline for export proceeds repatriation, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no surrender requirement. Export receivables may be held indefinitely in any freely convertible currency, and the Swiss AG may elect to keep foreign currency with a Swiss licensed bank or an offshore bank treasury account without SNB authorisation. For ISIC 6311 data-processing and video-match service exports, invoices may be issued in EUR, USD, CHF or any other currency, and converted to operating currency only when required by commercial need.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account (blocked for paid-in share capital) and Operational Treasury Account (multi-currency, with SEPA and SWIFT connectivity)

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Credit Suisse AG (a UBS Group company)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account and Operating Account, with dedicated digital-asset and cross-border payments advisory
Capital Escrow Account and Operational Account, strong presence in the Crypto Valley with FINMA-regulated custody capabilities
Local Operational and Escrow Account, best suited for cooperative-structured domestic subsidiaries
Operational Payments Account with SEPA Instant and Swiss Payment Standards access, not preferred for escrow or LC transactions

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Low-Medium for primary treasury use; Medium-High only as an ancillary collection and payout rail. A foreign/offshore EMI such as Revolut Business, Wise Business, or a UK/US-licensed EMI can be used to receive Apple IAP and Paymentwall settlements in major currencies, but the lawful and practical limitations for a Swiss AG are consequential. Such EMIs do not have a Swiss banking licence, cannot issue a Swiss clearing number, and cannot provide the notary-required blocked-capital certificate. They also do not fall within the Swiss deposit protection scheme, expose the AG to second-tier counterparty risk, and may not be recognised by FINMA as an acceptable AML-compliant custodian. If the EMI actively acquires Swiss clients or executes payments on behalf of the AG into Swiss bank accounts, it may trigger FINMA licensing under Art. 1b of the Swiss Banking Act or the FinSA/FinIA requirements. The compliant blueprint is to maintain a large-liquidity buffer in a FINMA-licensed commercial bank and use EMIs solely for low-balance international card collection and sub-1% cash-balance settlement.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is mandatory for effective onboarding in the majority of Tier-1 institutions. For a Swiss AG with non-resident UBOs and a Web3/social-app profile, at least two natural persons—typically the chairman and chief financial officer—must appear in person at the Swiss bank's branch or at a FINMA-regulated foreign correspondent bank with an identical AML attestation standard. Remote opening is legally permissible through video identification using a FINMA-recognised electronic verification system or a Switzerland-regulated fintech intermediary, but the bank retains residual discretion to require a physical board meeting if the corporate purpose is considered medium-risk or if the beneficial-ownership chain is opaque. For this particular project, the prudent strategy is physical appearance of the UBO and the key operational director, with notarised signatures and apostilles for all corporate documents.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk geography concentration in user payments or counterparty countries (e.g. Russia, Nigeria, regions with MONEYVAL/Egmont deficiencies).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide geo-blocking evidence, IP address intelligence, user country distribution report, platform terms prohibiting access from restricted jurisdictions, OFAC/SECO sanction-screen export, FATF/FACTA risk assessment, and a clear demonstration that high-risk traffic is technically and contractually prevented from generating revenue flows.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Transaction-flow mismatch between declared business model (video matching / social telephony) and actual payment settlement patterns (e.g. high-velocity micropayments, chargeback anomalies, use of unlicensed money-services instruments).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Deliver the audited historical Paymentwall/Apple IAP reconciliation, user journey documentation, in-app token/credit mechanics, refund policy, merchant agreement with payment processors, anti-fraud KYT transaction monitoring output, and an independent AML review confirming that payments correspond to real telephony services rather than money transmission.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear source of wealth for the CHF 100,000+ capital injection and doubts about shareholder funding from cryptocurrency or unregulated overseas trading.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide notarised share subscription agreements, personal bank statements of the shareholder, tax clearance certificate, FINMA-regulated conversion certificate if any crypto assets were liquidated, proof of transfer from a regulated digital-asset bank, and a sworn declaration of source of funds in accordance with the Swiss Code of Obligations.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Web3 / digital-asset nexus because the AG name or the product is associated with matchmaking tokens, NFTs, or decentralised markets, creating a presumption of unlicensed MSB activity.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide a FINMA classification legal opinion confirming that the in-app matching token is not a payment token, does not embody a claim against the issuer, and is not transferable outside the platform; evidence that treasury flows are entirely fiat in nature; segregation of any token operations into a separate regulated entity; and ongoing compliance monitoring with FINMA circulars.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound share capital must be routed via SWIFT MT103 from the shareholder's bank to the Swiss AG's blocked escrow account at a FINMA-licensed bank. The sending bank must use a purpose code identifying the credit as a capital contribution (e.g. 'A020' under ISO 8583, or the Swiss bank's internal Einlagezahlung keyword) so that the receiving bank may release the no-debit confirmation to the notary. For a modern treasury setup, the preferred rail is SWIFT gpi (global payment innovation) with unique end-to-end transaction reference (UETR) and OPIC (optional payment instruction code) to avoid correspondent delays. The verified capital certificate issued by the bank, the notarial deed, and the Commercial Register excerpt must be retained in the treasury file. Amounts exceeding CHF 1 million may trigger a wealth-source questionnaire requiring personal balance sheet and tax documentation; capital in crypto is only acceptable if liquidated through a FINMA-regulated securities dealer with a full transfer trail and then delivered through normal fiat wire.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound disbursements for trade settlement should use the Swiss Payment Standards (SIC5) and SEPA Instant rails for euro-denominated flows, and SWIFT MT103/MT202 for USD, GBP and other non-SEPA currencies. For structured trade in the video-match vertical with potential licensing or content-conduit counterparts, a UCP600-compliant commercial letter of credit issued by UBS/ZKB and confirmed by an international bank provides documentary security. The bank will require the underlying commercial contract, tax invoice, and for cross-border service payments, a transfer pricing control certificate. Royalty, dividend and management fee outflows from the Swiss AG to the foreign parent should be tagged with the relevant OECD transaction purpose code on the SWIFT MT103, accompanied by a board minute, a cost-allocation statement, and the Swiss withholding tax certificate if relief is claimed under the DTT. For recurring settlement with Paymentwall and Apple, the AG should establish a direct debit / cash-pooling arrangement in USD and EUR with same-day sweep to avoid stranded balances.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: OTC FX outright forwards between CHF and EUR/USD with Swiss commercial banks or FINMA-regulated counterparties up to five-year maturity
FX swaps (swap points) for short-term liquidity management between CHF and USD/EUR
Cross-currency interest rate swaps (CCIRS) to convert floating-rate foreign-currency liabilities into CHF obligations
FX call/put options to protect foreign-currency revenue against adverse CHF appreciation

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for permitted emerging-market currencies (e.g. Nigerian naira, Vietnamese dong) executed through a Swiss/London prime broker, despite the fully convertible CHF status, because the AG may invoice in soft currencies

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual financial statements and ordinary shareholders' meeting approval
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Annual General Meeting of shareholders (no commercial register filing for a private AG); independent auditor if a statutory audit applies
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months of the financial year end (Art. 699 para. 3, Swiss Code of Obligations); for calendar-year companies, no later than 30 June of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: No direct administrative strike-off; non-approval or failure to prepare accounts triggers court-ordered audit, administrative penal measures under Art. 958f CO, and personal liability of directors for resulting damage.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Cantonal and federal corporate income and net wealth tax return (Steuererklärung)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cantonal tax administration and Swiss Federal Tax Administration (ESTV/AFC)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Set by the cantonal tax authorities on the return; commonly six months after fiscal year end (calendar-year company by 30 June), with extensions available
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Default interest at 4.5% per annum on outstanding taxes; late-filing penalty up to 30% of assessed tax; penal proceedings for tax evasion; no direct registry strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Swiss VAT return (Form 20) for quarterly or annual VAT tax period
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Swiss Federal Tax Administration, VAT Division (ESTV/AFC)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after the end of each VAT tax period; quarterly for most VAT-registered AGs, annual only if expressly approved by ESTV
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Default interest at 5% per annum; tax-associated fine under the VAT Act of 25% to 75% of evaded tax; debt-enforcement proceedings if tax remains unpaid.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual wage and social insurance declaration (AHV/AVS wage list and employer contribution statement)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cantonal AHV compensation fund (Ausgleichskasse) and supplementary social insurance carriers
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By 31 January following the calendar year for employee wage declarations; social insurance contribution invoices are issued quarterly
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Interest on unpaid contributions at 5% per annum; administrative fines and criminal prosecution for deliberate non-payment; director liability for wrongful use of withheld employee contributions.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under Art. 727 CO, an ordinary statutory audit is mandatory if, in two consecutive fiscal years, at least two of these thresholds are exceeded: balance sheet total CHF 20 million; sales revenue CHF 40 million; 250 full-time employees on average. Listed companies always require an ordinary audit. Other AGs require a limited audit; the audit may be waived entirely with unanimous shareholder approval and fewer than 10 full-time employees.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Swiss Code of Obligations (Art. 958–963) applied with Swiss GAAP FER; IFRS is permitted for individual statutory accounts and is required for the consolidated accounts of publicly traded groups under SIX listing rules.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Switzerland does not operate a public UBO register. The AG must maintain an Aktienbuch identifying registered shareholders and, where shares are held by nominees, the beneficial-owner information for AML purposes as required by the Anti-Money Laundering Act when banking or payment-service relationships are established. No annual UBO declaration or share-transfer confirmation is filed with the commercial register; changes in shareholding are recorded in the share register and board minutes. Commercial register filings are required only for events such as changes to directors, auditors, share capital or articles of incorporation.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Directors (Verwaltungsratsprotokolle and election records)
Minute Book (Minutes of General Meetings and Board Meetings)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 250–1,000 per annum depending on canton and service provider (CHF equivalent)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 3,000–12,000 per annum for a limited statutory audit of a small AG; ordinary audit fees are materially higher (CHF equivalent)

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 18.0% (federal effective rate 8.5% on pre-tax profit plus cantonal/communal rates averaging 10-13%)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Participation relief for qualifying dividends (95% exemption), deemed liquidated capital gains for tax-holiday companies, notional interest deduction (NID) in cantons applying its optional implementation, and R&D super-deduction in certain cantons

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Swiss federal tax return form (Formulaire / Fragebogen für die direkte Bundessteuer) filed via ESTV/eTax portal (eTax auf dem Portal Suissedeclare.ch)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Generally due within 6 months following the end of the business fiscal year; extended to 30 June of the following calendar year for December year-end companies unless extension granted

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Identification and legal form: company name, UID (Unternehmens-Identifikationsnummer), registered seat, and ISIC/NACE code
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident parent or foreign shareholder must be identified with foreign tax ID and country code; Swiss entity remains the taxpayer

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Profit determination statement: opening balance, net income per commercial accounts, extraordinary income, and reconciliation adjustments
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Adjustments must reflect arm's-length pricing of cross-border transactions with non-resident related parties

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable earnings before loss offset: statutory net profit as per Swiss Code of Obligations (OR 958) including accrued income
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: No foreign R&D expense allocation may be claimed unless documented under the exceptional R&D cost carve-out rules

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductions: business expenses, professional costs, depreciation, pension fund contributions, and prior-year tax losses
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Royalties and interest paid to foreign related parties require documentary evidence of beneficial ownership and economic substance

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Participation income: dividends, capital gains from qualifying shareholdings, and participation relief calculation
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Participation relief requires an active link with a permanent establishment abroad and no treaty-shopping arrangement

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax rate computation and creditable foreign tax credits (direct credits for foreign withholding taxes)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign branch losses and income must be evidenced by a certified permanent establishment tax return

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty of CHF 1,000-10,000 per incident; daily surcharge of up to CHF 500 after reminder; criminal fine up to CHF 100,000 for deliberate non-compliance; interest on late tax at statutory rate of 2-5% per annum

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 35% (federal anticipatory/withholding tax, refundable or creditable in accordance with DTA rules)
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Application must be submitted to the Swiss Federal Tax Administration (ESTV) on Form 820/821 with (i) certificate of residence (Form 822/823) issued by the foreign tax authority, (ii) TRC showing beneficial ownership, (iii) shareholding documentation confirming the holding period, and (iv) declaration of economic substance; application must be filed within 3 years of the distribution date for automatic relief or via refund procedure
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: statutory Swiss WHT at source generally 0% if no connection to a Swiss permanent establishment; treaty rates generally 0-10% depending on the double taxation agreement. Interest: statutory Swiss WHT at 35% on interest paid on bonds and bank deposits; treaty rates typically 0-10%; unilateral relief and per-domicile distinctions apply

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: No statutory fixed threshold in CHF; mandatory Local File and Master File preparation is endorsed by the OECD TP Guidelines and ordinance (e.g., when cross-border related-party transactions exceed CHF 500,000 annually or involve high-risk intangibles)
approved_arm_length_methodologies: CUP, Resale Price, Cost Plus, TNMM, Profit Split
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Swiss ESR rules applied through the existing substantial economic presence requirements for tax treaty benefits: activities must be performed, assets must be held, and risks must be managed in Switzerland for the benefit to be recognised; video-matching platform operators must demonstrate actual operation of matching algorithms, content moderation personnel, servers or relevant contracted infrastructure, and business decision-making in Switzerland

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: False statements in tax returns, concealed revenue from video-chat app subscriptions or virtual gifting, artificially low transfer prices routed through low-tax jurisdictions
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal fine up to CHF 250,000 (Federal Act on Direct Federal Tax Art. 175-186); recovery of unpaid tax plus compound interest; exclusion from participation relief
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly sign false filings are jointly and severally liable for the tax shortfall; may face disqualification as directors and, in aggravated cases, custodial sentence from 3 months to 2 years

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Swiss AG nominally holding digital platform contracts and treasury functions, but no staff, no physical server assets, no actual management in Switzerland, and no alignment with ESR for the video-matching service
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of DTA benefits, reassessment of income at full Swiss corporate tax rate, retroactive withholding at 35% on deemed distributions, and fines for failure to keep commercial books
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Civil piercing of the corporate veil under Swiss Code of Obligations Art. 754 (liability for breach of fiduciary duties) and Art. 757; travel bans under the Federal Act on Debt Collection, and prison sentences up to 5 years for fraudulent bankruptcy or misuse of the corporate form

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Video-chat platform used for money laundering through Apple IAP refunds, anonymous prepaid payment cards, or channelling illegal proceeds through Paymentwall without valid AML-KYC controls
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Swiss Anti-Money Laundering Act (VStrG/AMLA): registration with the Anti-Money Laundering Authority, administrative fines up to CHF 500,000, licence revocation for licensed financial intermediaries, asset freezing orders, and confiscation of illegally acquired corporate assets
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and operational officers may personally face criminal proceedings for money laundering (Art. 305bis StGB, imprisonment up to 3 years), aggravated money laundering (Art. 305quater StGB, imprisonment from 1 to 10 years), and civil compensation to damaged parties under Article 41 of the Swiss Code of Obligations

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to levy the statutory 35% anticipatory tax on dividends distributed to the non-resident parent or investor, or claiming a refund on an improperly documented TRC with no beneficial ownership substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal fine, mandatory payment of the withheld amount, penalty interest additionally payable at 5% per annum, and loss of refund or relief already granted
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The board members and responsible finance officers are personally liable for wilful failure to collect the tax, may be arrested upon leaving Switzerland, and can be sanctioned with imprisonment not exceeding 1 year (VStrG Art. 177)
